purpose: Free text-level accept/reject expectations for any product validator. Written by the reviewer from real saved drafts and my own paraphrases/adversarial items. Use the validator as the only judge; do not edit items to fit it. A reject item that passes, or an accept item that is rejected, is a recorded failure. No pass count means readiness.

items.text: If you pause the regular deposits, you won’t earn the ASP bonus for the months you don’t save. The bonus is only granted when the required monthly contribution is kept active. When you start saving again, the bonus can resume from the next qualifying month.
items.why: invented pause/resume rule; source says breaks allowed, deposits need not be consecutive

items.text: You can pause your ASP deposits whenever you need to. No bonus or interest is lost while you’re on a break; you’ll continue earning the regular 1 % deposit interest each year.
items.why: unsupported no-loss assurance (pause delays reaching 20 deposits)

items.text: If your savings exceed 5 000 € on 1 January 2027, a premature lump-sum withdrawal without the higher tax rate is allowed only for specific reasons (divorce, spouse’s death, serious illness, prolonged unemployment). Without one of those reasons, any withdrawal will be taxed at the normal 30% capital-gains rate on the amount withdrawn.
items.why: source: above threshold, no higher rate only with a reason; so without a reason the higher rate applies, not the normal rate

items.text: Yes, the €5,000 limit refers to the maximum amount you can deduct from tax on your PS-account contributions each year.
items.why: answers 'same as withdrawal threshold?' with yes; merges the two 5,000 figures

items.text: Yes, the €5 000 limit for PS contributions is the same amount you can deduct from tax each year. It’s the tax-deduction cap, not a separate saving limit.
items.why: same merge, omits the 1 Jan 2027 balance test

items.text: Whether you can still claim the 2026 contribution deduction depends on the historic test – you must have had no more than 5 000 € in total PS savings on 1 January 2027.

items.text: ASP loans need 20 monthly deposits and 4 percent savings.
Stopping for a few months just means the bonus pauses, then it carries on once you restart.

If your PS savings are 5 000 € or less on 1 January 2027, you can withdraw the whole amount in 2027 or 2028 without the higher tax rate. The normal 30 % capital‑gains tax still applies, and the option isn’t available if you’ve already reached retirement age and have started scheduled PS withdrawals.

The tax deduction for PS‑account contributions ends at the start of 2027. You can still deduct up to 5 000 € of your payments in 2026. Savings that were already in the account before 1 January 2027 keep their existing tax treatment.
items.source: R7-0 real draft (first paragraph; the rest of that draft's final sentence was looser)

items.text: An ASP account is a home‑savings account for first‑time buyers. You can save at your own pace and, after at least 20 monthly deposits, you become eligible for an ASP loan. You earn 1 % annual deposit interest, added each 31 December, and a 4 % bonus interest once you have the required deposits and take out a loan. The bonus applies for the year you start saving and the next five calendar years.

No. The €5,000 tax deduction and the €5,000 withdrawal limit are two separate rules. The deduction applies to contributions, not to the existing balance; the withdrawal figure refers to your total PS savings on 1 Jan 2027, and a 5,000 balance today does not by itself settle either.

The 4 % bonus is paid in arrears once you have made 20 approved monthly deposits and take out an ASP loan or a regular home loan to buy a home. The 10 % savings share is a condition for applying for an ASP loan, not a prerequisite for the bonus with a regular loan.
Pausing just delays reaching 20 monthly deposits. The bonus conditions (20 approved deposits and a home loan) still apply, and the deposits don’t need to be consecutive.
You earn 1 % annual deposit interest on your ASP savings, added on 31 December.
To apply for an ASP loan, your ASP savings must cover at least 10 % of the home’s price, or 10 % of your share if you buy together.
Above 5,000 euros on 1 January 2027, an early withdrawal avoids the higher tax rate only if you have a specific reason such as divorce, a spouse’s death, serious illness or prolonged unemployment.
If you have both reached retirement age and your planned PS withdrawals have started, you can’t take it all out at once.
The page doesn’t say what happens if you have reached retirement age but your planned withdrawals haven’t started, so I can’t tell you.
You mentioned 5,000 euros. The PS withdrawal test looks at your total savings on 1 January 2027, so today’s balance alone doesn’t decide it.
